title: '22 built-in agents' count and list are obsolete
reality: v2.3.0 moved all optional agents out of the base Engine into downloadable packages ('Reduced the base Engine by removing more than 25,000 lines of optional agent, map, call, and table-game implementation code'). Verified upstream: BUILT_IN_AGENT_MANIFESTS in packages/shared/src/features/agents/agent-registry.generated.ts is now an EMPTY array — there are zero bundled built-in agents. BUILT_IN_AGENT_IDS (packages/shared/src/types/agent.ts) still lists 21 legacy ids (about-me-keeper removed), but these are compatibility identifiers for the now-downloadable official packages, not shipped agents. Fresh installs contain no optional agents (2.3.0).
fix: Rewrite agents.md's 'Built-In Agents' section (lines 51-87) as 'Official Downloadable Agents'. Delete the '22 built-in agents' claim and the instruction to count BUILT_IN_AGENT_MANIFESTS (now empty). Keep the per-agent descriptions but state that every one of these agents is now an installable package from the official catalog, with BUILT_IN_AGENT_IDS retained only as legacy/compatibility ids.

title: about-me-keeper is retired, not the '22nd built-in'
reality: Verified upstream: 'about-me-keeper' now appears in RETIRED_BUILT_IN_AGENT_IDS (packages/shared/src/types/agent.ts) and was removed from BUILT_IN_AGENT_IDS. Per 2.3.0, Conversation's About Me profile and the update_about_me tool 'remain built into the Engine and are not downloadable agents' (they are not agents at all); per 2.3.2, About Me drafting moved from per-editor AI Write controls to Professor Mari, who writes the bio and saves it directly to the About Me field.
fix: Remove the about-me-keeper entry from the agent list (line 83) and add 'about-me-keeper' to the retired list at line 55. Add a note that Conversation About Me is now an Engine-built-in feature (update_about_me tool) drafted via Professor Mari, not an agent.

title: Downloadable-agents architecture (Download Agents library) undocumented
reality: 2.3.0 added a full-page Agents → Download Agents library for installing, reading about, updating, and uninstalling official capability packages, grouped installed/uninstalled and ordered Writer, Tracker, Misc Agents, with creator artwork and Agents-star fallback. Install All / Uninstall All controls run through a safe sequential queue with progress and partial-failure reporting (2.3.0). 2.3.2 (#3676) added Conversation/Roleplay/Game compatibility badges and catalog search by supported mode. Fresh installs contain no optional agents; existing installs migrate agents and chat feature selections without losing settings, runtime data, or history (2.3.0).
fix: Add a new top-level section 'Downloadable Agents' near the top of agents.md describing the Download Agents library, Writer/Tracker/Misc groupings, Install All/Uninstall All, mode compatibility badges, and the fresh-install-is-empty + migration behavior. Update the intro line 5 ('All agents are disabled by default') to add that on v2.3+ fresh installs agents must first be INSTALLED from Download Agents before they can be enabled.

title: Pasta-Devs/Marinara-Agents 29-package catalog repo missing
reality: 2.3.0 published first-party downloadable agents in the Pasta-Devs/Marinara-Agents repository as individually verified packages, and added 'a canonical 29-package catalog summary to both Professor Mari prompt paths'. Verified from that repo's README: 29 first-party packages for Engine v2.3.0+ — 6 Writer (card-evolution-auditor, continuity, knowledge-retrieval, knowledge-router, director, prose-guardian), 8 Tracker (background, character-tracker, custom-tracker, expression, hierarchical-maps, persona-stats, quest, world-state), 15 Misc (eightball, chess, combat, conversation-calls, cyoa, echo-chamber, haptic, illustrator, html, lorebook-keeper, spotify/Music DJ, poker, rock-paper-scissors, tic-tac-toe, uno). Package ids match the old built-in ids (Music DJ is still 'spotify').
fix: In the new Downloadable Agents section, cite github.com/Pasta-Devs/Marinara-Agents as the official catalog repo and reproduce the 29-package breakdown (6 Writer / 8 Tracker / 15 Misc) with category assignment per agent (e.g. Card Evolution Auditor = Writer, Hierarchical Maps = Tracker). Tag each agent entry in the existing per-agent list with its category and package id.

title: Enable Agents master toggle semantics undocumented
reality: Each chat has an 'Enable Agents' master switch. 2.3.0 (#3669) preserved it during the v2.3 capability migration so upgrading cannot silently reactivate selected agents or their model calls. 2.3.3 made Hierarchical Maps obey each chat's Enable Agents toggle across Roleplay and Game UI, prompt generation, lorebook previews, retries, tracker state patches, session carryover, and checkpoints — disabled chats no longer initialize or call Maps services. 2.3.2 (#3692) gates custom-agent execution in all modes on this toggle.
fix: Add an 'Enable Agents master toggle' subsection: per-chat master switch that gates all agent initialization and model calls (including package-owned services like Hierarchical Maps); note it survives version migrations without re-enabling agents.

title: Custom-agent mode availability is stale (Conversation now included)
reality: agents.md's 'Game Mode & mode gating' section only documents v2.0 Game-Mode custom-agent selection. 2.3.2 (#3692) 'Allowed selected custom agents to run in Conversation, Roleplay, and Game chats whenever Enable Agents is on, while preserving per-mode availability rules for official packages.'
fix: Update the 'Game Mode & mode gating' section (line 139): selected custom agents now run in Conversation, Roleplay, and Game whenever the chat's Enable Agents toggle is on; modeAllowlist gating continues to apply to official packages only.

title: Hierarchical Maps package undocumented
reality: 2.3.0 moved Hierarchical Maps into an optional package (Tracker Agent, package id hierarchical-maps) enablable as an agent in Roleplay and during/after Game creation. 2.3.2 (#3679) moved its controls inside its active entry in Chat Settings → Agents (no separate top-level settings section). 2.3.3: obeys Enable Agents; incompatible Maps 1.0.x runtimes are quarantined before the database adapter loads (fixes recurring 't.select is not a function' crash); #3723 one-time correction removes the v2.3.2 migration's accidental auto-selection of Maps in every Roleplay/VN/Game chat; a fix stopped inactive-Maps calls causing 'Failed to flush 1 game-state patch callback' send-blocking errors.
fix: Add a Hierarchical Maps entry under Tracker Agents: optional downloadable package, available in Roleplay and Game, settings nested inside its Chat Settings → Agents entry, gated by Enable Agents, with the 1.0.x quarantine and #3723 migration-correction notes as troubleshooting context.

title: Calls (Conversation Calls) package undocumented
reality: 2.3.0 moved Conversation audio/video calls into an optional package (Misc, package id conversation-calls) and made Local Whisper a Calls-owned download — uninstalling Calls removes every downloaded Whisper model and its saved selection; Connections shows Local Speech Model controls only while Calls is installed. 2.3.2 (#3676) renamed user-facing references to 'Calls' (package IDs and legacy symbols preserved); #3685 package v1.0.4 stopped persisting a hardcoded assistant reply on generation failure and no longer requires provider-native JSON mode; #3671 fixed Whisper model discovery when DATA_DIR was unset.
fix: Add a 'Calls' entry (Misc agent, package id conversation-calls): live audio/video calls, mic transcription, character video presence; Calls owns Local Whisper model downloads (removed on uninstall); note the user-facing rename from 'Conversation Calls' to 'Calls'.

title: Table games are Conversation feature packages, not pipeline agents
reality: 2.3.0 moved UNO, Chess, Poker, 8-Ball Pool, Tic-Tac-Toe, and Rock-Paper-Scissors into optional packages with package-owned server runtimes. A 2.3.0 fix made installed Conversation feature packages stop behaving like per-chat pipeline agents: the six table games appear in Commands controls without separate Add Agent entries and expose surfaces/command runtimes without legacy activeAgentIds metadata. 2.3.2 (#3699) made installed Conversation games appear immediately in slash-command autocomplete and activate/deactivate contributions without an Engine restart, while route-bearing packages retain a safe restart path.
fix: Document the six table-game packages (eightball, chess, poker, tic-tac-toe, uno, rock-paper-scissors) as Conversation feature packages with slash commands (/8ball, /chess, /poker, /tictactoe, /uno, /rps) that surface under Commands controls — not per-chat pipeline agents — and note the no-restart activation vs restart-required route-bearing distinction.

title: Illustrator is now an install-gated package
reality: Illustrator is now an optional downloadable Misc package. 2.3.0: /illustrate and /selfie commands and image/video generation settings are hidden until Illustrator is installed; Gallery generation controls (Illustrate, Selfie, Storyboard, Video, Animate, Background) require Illustrator installed AND enabled for that chat in every mode; selfie configuration was renamed 'Illustrator Settings' in Chat Settings → Agents; Game setup's 'Visual Generation' was renamed Illustrator and its controls appear only when the package is installed; the Connections 'Illustrator' defaults category was renamed 'Images'. 2.3.2: a fix made package-owned commands (e.g. Selfies) appear as soon as the agent is installed.
fix: Update the illustrator entry (line 77): mark it a downloadable Misc package and add the gating behavior — /illustrate, /selfie, and all Gallery generation actions require the package installed and enabled per chat; mention the 'Illustrator Settings' and Connections 'Images' renames.

title: Music DJ is now an install-gated package with a third provider
reality: spotify (Music DJ) is now an optional downloadable Misc package. 2.3.0: enabling the always-available Music Player toggle without Music DJ installed shows 'Download Music DJ Agent to configure' guidance with a direct Download Agents action. The catalog describes Music DJ as playing scene-matched music through Spotify, YouTube, or local Game Assets — agents.md only documents Spotify and YouTube via musicProvider.
fix: Update the spotify/Music DJ entry (line 80): downloadable Misc package (id remains 'spotify'); Music Player toggle without the package installed shows download guidance; supported sources are Spotify, YouTube, and local Game Assets.

title: Startup auto-upgrade and package trust/lifecycle undocumented
reality: 2.3.1: installed official agents and feature packages check the Marinara-Agents catalog during server startup and automatically upgrade to the newest compatible version before their runtimes activate; offline/incompatible/missing/failed updates leave the previous version available; verified server-runtime failures roll back automatically. Catalog README: Engine validates catalog schema, checks version compatibility, verifies archive SHA-256 and per-file hashes/sizes, rejects unsafe paths, installs atomically; installed packages remain available offline; server-capability packages require restart when their runtime changes. 2.3.2 (#3706/#3707): catalog HTTP failures now report actual status instead of a blanket internet-outage diagnosis.
fix: Add a 'Package lifecycle' subsection covering startup auto-upgrade with rollback, offline availability of installed packages, checksum-verified atomic installs, and restart-on-runtime-change semantics.

title: Per-Engine-major catalog lanes undocumented
reality: 2.3.3 (#3712) added compatibility-aware official Agent catalog selection so each Engine major installs and updates only from its matching catalog lane. Verified in the Marinara-Agents repo: Engine 2 uses catalog/v2/catalog.json, Engine 3 uses catalog/v3/catalog.json, and catalog/catalog.json remains the legacy Engine 2 alias; each Engine release sees only packages compatible with its major version.
fix: In the Downloadable Agents / package lifecycle section, note the per-major catalog lanes (catalog/v2 vs catalog/v3, legacy alias) and that installs/updates are restricted to the Engine's matching lane (2.3.3 #3712).

title: Capability API 1.3 host services undocumented
reality: 2.3.2 (#3690) added capability API 1.3 host services for downloadable packages: safe model routing, persistence, history/checkpoints, resources, logging, transactions, client contribution loading, and visible readiness/retry states. 2.3.0 replaced the removed 25k lines with 'small validated capability registries and compatibility bridges' in the base Engine; 2.3.2 (#3647) made capability-owned file-table/column objects resolve through registered schema names and quarantined incompatible installed package versions before their hooks can crash generation.
fix: Add a short 'Capability API' subsection for people building/debugging packages: base Engine exposes capability registries + compatibility bridges; capability API 1.3 host services list; incompatible package versions are quarantined rather than allowed to crash generation.

title: Source-of-truth pointer omits package-owned agent code
reality: agents.md line 7 points only at Engine paths (all still exist upstream — verified agent-executor.ts, agent-pipeline.ts, agent.schema.ts, agent-prompts.ts return 200), but since 2.3.0 the feature implementations of optional agents live in the Marinara-Agents repo, not the Engine tree (e.g. Hierarchical Maps source under packages/hierarchical-maps/src/engine/, per that repo's README); the Engine registry file it points to for counting built-ins now contains an empty array. BuiltInAgentMeta also gained new fields: category ('writer'|'tracker'|'misc') and execution ('pipeline'|'feature').
fix: Update line 7: keep the Engine paths for the executor/pipeline/schema, add Pasta-Devs/Marinara-Agents (packages/<id>/manifest.json and package-owned src) as the source of truth for individual official agents, and remove/replace the agent-registry.generated.ts counting instruction. Mention the new category and execution manifest fields.

title: UI Location section describes pre-2.3 Agents panel
reality: agents.md's UI Location says the Agents Panel 'shows built-in agents (with toggles...)'. Since 2.3.0, agent sections, settings, and package-owned command toggles appear only for agents that are actually installed; Chat Settings → Agents remains available in Conversation, Roleplay, and Game even with no optional agents installed (built-in Conversation commands stay configurable); empty Roleplay/Game sections and the empty setup-wizard Agents step link directly to Download Agents; uninstalling an agent now removes its card from the open sidebar immediately (2.3.0 fix); downloaded package artwork is applied to installed agents in the sidebar.
fix: Rewrite the UI Location section (lines 235-237): Agents sidebar shows installed agents only, plus the Download Agents entry point; Chat Settings → Agents shows sections only for installed agents with empty states linking to Download Agents.

title: Combat agent vs new Tactical Combat Mode conflation risk
reality: The combat agent is now a downloadable Misc package ('Manages combat encounters, initiative, HP tracking, and turn-based actions' per catalog). Separately, 2.3.0 added a Game-mode 'Combat Preference' / 'Combat Style' setting with a new Tactical Combat Mode (grid battlefield, deterministic seeded engine, four difficulty levels) — a Game-mode engine feature, not the combat agent.
fix: Update the combat entry (line 65): note it is a downloadable Misc package, and add one line distinguishing it from Game mode's built-in Tactical Combat Mode (Combat Preference in setup wizard / Chat Settings → Combat Style) so users don't attribute tactical battles to the agent.
